prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell); normalizes Flight Intent Message vs Airport Capacity Plan. Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT (Target Off Block Time) only if capacity/ground path allow; conditional if handling late; frozen at horizon unless recorded exception/override. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; triggers arrival regulation when inbound demand exceeds Airport Acceptance Rate (AAR) in horizon); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; candidate AAR per runway config with basis shown on Common Situation Display); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT, Calculated Takeoff Time; Ground Delay Program for large imbalance); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; TOBT protecting CTT; CTT to TSM; withholds push while pad queue over threshold); North/South Runway Meter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display; deicing records; presents arrival plan to Aircraft Operator Representatives); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf); Gate Conflict Detector (Gate Reopening Memo); Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (option evaluation using runway, sector load, stand readiness, weather; alerts before holding stacks form); Sector Load Monitor (early terminal-sector overload warnings); Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; Fuel Truck Hold Advice); Collaborative Decision Log (decisions, arrival-plan acknowledgements); Audit Event Ledger; Performance Analytics Warehouse (planned treatment throughput vs pad occupancy, departure compliance); Handling Resource Planner; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard; updates arrival model); Business Rules Registry (queue thresholds, protected flight criteria); Identity Access Service; Digital Briefing Room. Modes: Normal Operations (prefer minor time-based sequence adjustment, delay upstream not airborne); Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase; Winter Operating Mode. Primary objective: prevent airborne holding. Restriction notice bounds regulation timeline before new landing rates; Flow Manager may apply tactical landing-rate reduction for defined review interval. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin); Slot Coordinator (Halcyon; distributes arrival times); Airline Operations Coordinator (AOC, Saffron; network impact review); Aircraft Operator Representative; Tower Supervisor (confirms landing rate); Airspace Sector Planner (confirms sector loads); Duty Manager; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Ramp Control Lead (verifies pad order).

New part:
S411: If conditions improve, the Regional Flow Manager may approve a staged landing-rate increase, but the increase is limited until the Tower Sequence Manager confirms stable spacing and runway occupancy performance.
S412: Diversion triggers are monitored continuously and include predicted holding beyond operator fuel thresholds, loss of required approach capability, sustained sector saturation, and runway availability below the minimum safe acceptance rate.
S413: The Network Operations Liaison coordinates with affected airline control centers when diversion risk becomes material so that alternate airport decisions can be made before fuel margins become critical.
S414: The Emergency Response Coordinator is informed when a diversion trigger is associated with an aircraft condition that could affect rescue and firefighting readiness at Meridian or at an alternate airport.
S415: During Adverse Weather Mode, tactical adjustments are reviewed more frequently because landing-rate stability may depend on short-lived runway configuration and approach spacing opportunities.
S416: During Capacity Reduction State, the Regional Flow Manager may combine arrival regulation with departure metering to protect surface balance and prevent inbound aircraft from occupying gates needed for recovery flights.
S417: All rate changes, rejected options, coordination outcomes, and effective times are written to the Audit Event Ledger for later review.
S418: The Performance Analytics Warehouse uses the recorded regulation history to compare predicted holding, actual airborne delay, diversion outcomes, and achieved landing rates for continuous improvement of Meridian arrival management.
S419: The Integrated Tactical Management Position is the primary workstation for real-time coordination of Meridian departure flow, arrival flow, airport capacity, and airspace constraints.
S420: It presents a combined tactical view so that the Regional Flow Manager can compare planned demand, measured throughput, and active control measures without changing applications.
S421: The Common Situation Display provides the base map, timeline, flight list, and measure status panels used at the position.
S422: The Regional Flow Platform synchronizes the tactical display with the Time Synchronization Service so that all timestamps, countdowns, and validity intervals use the same operational clock.
S423: The Arrival Regulation Console is also known as Nightjar at the Integrated Tactical Management Position, where the alias is displayed only in operator profile help text.
S424: Arrival demand is monitored against the Airport Acceptance Rate, current sequencing performance, and any Ground Delay Program that remains in effect.
S425: The Tower Supervisor uses the display to see runway assignment pressure, airborne sequence spacing, and expected crossing points at the North Runway Meter and the South Runway Meter.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
